title: Chocolate Hearts Box

drivers.name: Holiday: Labor Day
drivers.evidence: Past Labor Day weeks show inconsistent effects (x0.69, x1.15); one with concurrent promotion. Noise-adjusted estimate is x1.0. No repeat pattern. No reliable uplift.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 8.7. Labor Day (Mon) is a known driver, but past effect was x0.69 (2024) and x1.15 (2025 with concurrent 10% promo). The 2025 Labor Day week had a promotion, so it's not clean. The 2024 effect is isolated and not replicated. Noise-adjusted estimate is x1.0. No price change. No promotion this week. Recent back-to-school season shows no lift. The uplift model suggests 1.00, and our evidence confirms no clear signal. No driver justifies moving the median. Spread remains baseline.

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:

  shelf price: 10.15 (+0.0% vs regular price 10.15)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 8.7 | 5%-95%: 3.0 - 15.4 | 10%-90%: 3.4 - 14.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-67% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
